rounds.text: Adani Power Ltd is trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic worth, backed by a discounted cash flow model showing an intrinsic value of Rs 307 per share against its current market price of Rs 208, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 32.2% [E46, E47]. Furthermore, the company's reverse DCF reveals that the current market price only implies a 12.7% earnings growth, which sits comfortably below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E48]. Profitability and capital efficiency metrics far outpace broader sector benchmarks, highlighted by a robust ROE of 19.76% compared to a sector median of 7.28% and an ROCE of 15.08% versus a sector benchmark of 7.38% [E9, E10]. Operational momentum is strong, demonstrated by a 15% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months, a quarterly operating margin of 42% in June 2026, and cash generation that fully backs reported profits with an operating cash flow of Rs 20,514 Cr [E21, E31, E34, E35]. Conceded: [E4], [E36], [E62].

Adani Power Ltd carries significant financial and valuation risks that are starkly highlighted by a negative free cash flow of Rs -2,817 Cr in March 2026 [E36], alongside a massive surge in borrowings to Rs 54,670 Cr [E40] and a staggering 189.6% jump in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 35,053 Cr [E41]. This heavy capex build-up phase coincides with a negative flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E62], while reporting zero dividend yield despite repeated profits [E4, E61]. Valuation multiples also appear overextended relative to traditional anchors, with a price-to-book ratio of 6.17x [E2], a P/E of 28.2x [E1] trading at a premium to sector benchmarks [E6, E7], and a signal engine warning that recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 49% [E58]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship shows cracks as foreign institutional holdings dropped from 17.51% in September 2023 to 11.76% in June 2026 [E43], and the screening engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E68]. Investors also face extreme volatility risks, evidenced by an annualized volatility of 54.1% [E55] and a terrifying worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.2% [E54]. Conceded: the company boasts a robust return on equity track record with a 3-year median of 31.8% [E60] and operating cash flows fully backed by profits at 1.58x conversion [E34].

However, this capital expenditure build-up represents growth spend underway to capture robust sector tailwinds [E41, E69], and operating cash flows of Rs 20,514 Cr fully back reported profits with a healthy 1.58x cash conversion rate [E34, E35]. Conceded: earnings growth is flagged as decelerating [E68] and price growth has outpaced profit growth [E58], but the business still delivered strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 58% [E19] and robust TTM profit growth of 15% [E21]. While the bull justifies negative free cash flow of Rs -2,817 Cr [E36] with growth spending [E41], the massive increase in borrowings to Rs 54,670 Cr [E40] is particularly concerning given the warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E62]. Conceded: promoter holdings [E42] and domestic institutional stakes [E44] have risen, but this is overshadowed by the substantial 5.75 percentage point retreat of foreign institutions to a reduced holding of 11.76% [E43]. The bull's focus on high return metrics [E9][E60] ignores that the stock trades at a price-to-book of 6.17x [E2], which is vastly overextended compared to the sector benchmark of 1.68x [E7]. Despite historical profit growth [E19], the bull fails to address that current earnings growth is decelerating [E68] while price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 49% [E58]. Finally, the total absence of dividends [E4][E61] leaves investors with no yield to buffer against an annualised volatility of 54.1% [E55] and a historical record of drawdowns as severe as -89.2% [E54].
